title: Welcome To The Jungle Just Dropped Its Trailer. Thirty Stars, One Jungle, Zero Subtlety. We're In.
excerpt: Akshay Kumar leads Bollywood's most absurdly stacked ensemble in the Welcome franchise's wildest chapter yet — arriving in cinemas June 26.
body:
The trailer for **Welcome To The Jungle** landed on Wednesday and it is, by any reasonable measure, four minutes and ten seconds of pure, unfiltered Bollywood excess. There are at least thirty recognizable faces on screen at any given moment. There is a jungle. There is a fake film set inside that jungle. There is **Jacqueline Fernandez**, who went full Paris Hilton blonde for the role because **Akshay Kumar** apparently told her to. And there is **Arshad Warsi**, inheriting the sacred legacy of Majnu Bhai's painting, which might be the most emotionally significant prop transfer in Hindi cinema history.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=R704yP3dlXw</youtube>

This is Welcome 3. Subtlety was never invited.

## The Setup Is Gloriously Unhinged

Directed by **Ahmed Khan**, the film drops its ensemble into a jungle where a fictional movie is supposedly being shot — except the danger turns out to be very, very real. Akshay plays a struggling film actor, which is already funnier than it should be given that he headlines roughly four releases a year. The actresses in the film are written as being wildly insecure about each other. There's a light jab at the industry's casting culture. And then everything explodes into the kind of slapstick chaos that the franchise has turned into an art form.

The trailer leans hard into nostalgia. The Majnu Bhai painting callback alone had fans losing it within minutes of release. The original 2007 **Welcome** — starring **Akshay Kumar**, **Nana Patekar**, **Anil Kapoor**, and **Katrina Kaif** — became a cult comedy that still gets quoted at family gatherings and WhatsApp groups. The sequel, **Welcome Back** (2015), had its moments. This third installment is clearly going bigger, louder, and more populated than either predecessor.

## The Cast List Is Its Own Movie

Let's just acknowledge what we're dealing with here. The film stars **Akshay Kumar**, **Suniel Shetty**, **Paresh Rawal**, **Raveena Tandon**, **Jacqueline Fernandez**, **Disha Patani**, **Arshad Warsi**, **Jackie Shroff**, **Lara Dutta**, **Farida Jalal**, **Johnny Lever**, **Rajpal Yadav**, **Shreyas Talpade**, **Tusshar Kapoor**, **Krushna Abhishek**, **Kiku Sharda**, **Daler Mehndi**, **Aftab Shivdasani**, **Urvashi Rautela**, and roughly fifteen other actors who each probably got three days of shooting and a trailer mention.

The Akshay-Suniel reunion is the real headline. Their chemistry — forged in **Hera Pheri** (2000) and its sequel — remains one of Bollywood's most reliable comic engines. Every time they share the screen, something lands. Throw in Paresh Rawal playing a delusional filmmaker and you've essentially assembled the holy trinity of Hindi comedy.

> "Film? Bilkul Fake! Danger? Ekdum Real! Survival Skills? Zero!" — Official tagline

## Jacqueline's Blonde Moment

One of the more delightful revelations from the promotional cycle: **Jacqueline Fernandez** going blonde for the film. In a recent interview, she revealed that it was Akshay himself who convinced her to make the switch. "You need to be Paris Hilton blonde," he reportedly told her. And she went for it — a commitment to character that, in the context of a Welcome film, feels both completely unnecessary and absolutely perfect.

## The Diaspora Play

Welcome films have always been NRI comfort food. They're the movies you watch with your parents when everyone's home for the holidays. They require zero intellectual engagement and deliver maximum laughs per minute. For the Indian diaspora in the US, UK, and Canada, Welcome To The Jungle releasing on **June 26** — right in the middle of summer break — is near-perfect timing.

The film releases internationally through **Marudhar Entertainment**, which means it'll be playing at your local AMC or Cineplex if it has even a modest desi population nearby. Given the franchise's track record, expect packed Thursday night shows in Edison, Fremont, Brampton, and Hounslow.

## Should You Care?

Look, nobody walks into a Welcome film expecting cinema. You walk in expecting your uncle's favorite jokes delivered by professionals, a plot that makes no sense and doesn't need to, and at least two dance numbers that have no business being as catchy as they are. The trailer suggests Welcome To The Jungle delivers exactly that — amplified to a scale that borders on parody.

The franchise has always understood something fundamental about its audience: sometimes you don't want to think. Sometimes you just want to laugh until your stomach hurts, surrounded by people who are laughing just as hard. If the trailer is any indication, June 26 might be one of those nights.

Bring your whole family. Leave your film criticism at home.
